title: msa-ad: Measurement System Analysis for Automated-Driving Validation
description:
A Python implementation of Measurement System Analysis (MSA) methods applied to automated-driving validation benches.

The package provides two groups of analyses. Bench characterisation decomposes the variation in a bench result into scenario, bench and repeatability components: crossed ANOVA gage repeatability and reproducibility (Gage R&R) with %GRR and number of distinct categories for continuous safety-margin metrics such as minimum time-to-collision; bias and linearity studies against reference values; and attribute agreement analysis with Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa and Wilson confidence intervals for binary pass/fail verdicts, where a variance decomposition is not applicable. Coverage-claim verification runs a catalogue of seeded known faults through the production test campaign and reports the measured detection rate, with Wilson intervals, against any claimed coverage figure.

The intended application is simulation, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) and fault-injection test benches used in automated-driving validation. The statistical methods follow the AIAG Measurement Systems Analysis reference manual, 4th edition.

Requires Python 3.10 or later. Depends only on numpy, scipy and pandas. The test suite asserts the computed variance components, kappa statistics and confidence intervals against independently known values.

This is a proposed method and a reference implementation. It is not a standard and has not been validated against industrial data; see the repository README for the full statement of status and limitations.
